European Commission (2007). Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control: Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Ceramic Manufacturing Industry, August 2007. European IPPC Bureau, Joint Research Centre, Seville. No DOI or report number printed.

Targeted pass of the 260-page Ceramics BREF (August 2007). Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 28). Loaded (main file, 63 technologies): kiln and dryer specific energy per t product from the Chapter 2 operating-data tables and Chapter 3 consumption data - bricks/roof tiles (Table 2.2 tunnel kilns, Table 2.4 fast-firing tunnel kilns, intermittent kilns text, Table 3.10 Austrian natural gas/electricity and Spanish totals per installation), vitrified clay pipes (Table 2.7; Table 3.13 drying and firing by pipe size), refractories (Tables 2.9-2.12 chamber/tunnel dryers, tunnel and shuttle kilns; Table 3.17 drying+firing), expanded clay rotary kiln firing per m3, wall and floor tiles (Table 2.14, Table 3.31 tunnel vs roller once/twice fired, Table 3.32 Italian spray drying/drying/firing gas and electricity, spray-drying and tile-drying text ranges), porcelain tableware (Tables 2.17-2.18), sanitaryware (Tables 2.21-2.23, Table 3.45 conventional vs fibre-insulated tunnel, roller, shuttle), electrical insulator shuttle kiln; Table 3.5 total CO2 emission factor of porous-clay-block tunnel kilns (149 kg/t); combined heat recycling brickworks (Sect. 4.1.2); emerging techniques (radiant-tube burners, microwave firing, internal-heating drying of refractory components, Ch. 6). Not loaded: all pollutant (dust, NOx, SOx, HF, HCl, VOC, metals) data, BAT-AELs, water, waste, noise and the flue-gas cleaning cost tables (Table 4.7, Sect. 4.2-4.3); EMS costs; cogeneration (no numbers). No cost figure for any whole kiln or dryer is printed; the only technology cost (radiant tubes, a lower bound mixing capex and opex) is in _measures. Sector statistics (Tables 1.2, 1.7, 3.11), whole-plant energy of single plants (Tables 3.40, 3.46, 3.52, 3.55) and step energies of non-thermal steps are in _other-values. Traps: many Chapter 2 values are 'drying + firing' (stated in each note) - scope wider than the kiln; Table 2.14 header layout (tunnel vs roller columns) read from setting densities; Table 2.18 one column is 'without drying'; Table 3.13 electricity is on a primary-energy basis (other-values); tile drying 250-750 kJ/kg is LHV, every other energy value has no stated heating-value basis; most kJ/kg figures carry no carrier split (target fuel; mainly natural gas); intermittent brick kilns printed at 500-900 kJ/kg look implausibly low (loaded, flagged). Nearly all numbers are reprinted from UBA 2001, BMLFUW 2003, TWG Ceramics 2005, CERAME-UNIE 2003 or Timellini 2004 and flagged in notes.
